summary: I confirmed the claim. In episode 1, Jev chose which coin to walk to at each decision. The agent touched three coins, and each time leaderstats Coins went up by that coin's "Value" attribute and the coin was removed: 0→1 (Coin1, value 1), 1→3 (Coin3, value 2), 3→4 (Coin2, value 1). This matches CoinGame.server.luau, where touching a coin adds its Value (1 if it has none) and then destroys the coin. I made no direct changes to the game, either in the episode or in the one probe, which only read values. The game logged one error at start (Workspace.Sign.SignText:3, "attempt to index nil with 'TextLabel'"), which has nothing to do with coins. The harness also hit two errors of its own: it tried to read the position of a coin the game had just removed. That cost a couple of updates but didn't change the coin counts recorded.
evidence: t=5.63 Coin1 (Value 1) touched and removed: Coins 0 -> 1
t=11.48 Coin3 (Value 2) touched and removed: Coins 1 -> 3
t=19.77 Coin2 (Value 1) touched and removed: Coins 3 -> 4
Jev made 11 decisions; each time it chose among 2-3 coin options (touch_coin_1/2), and all 3 options it started worked ('coin taken')
Game log: one error at t=0, Workspace.Sign.SignText:3 attempt to index nil with 'TextLabel' (not related to coins), plus an asset-type warning
findings: Workspace.Sign.SignText:3 throws 'attempt to index nil with TextLabel' when the game starts (from the game's error log, t=0.0)
